exposure: Presence of a 'rail sign' on ultrasound
outcome: Risk of abnormally invasive placenta (placenta increta or percreta)
Probability of perioperative approaches (preoperative vascular control, uterine artery embolization)
Risk of adverse clinical outcomes (blood transfusion, admission to the intensive care unit, hysterectomy, bladder invasion)
cohort: 133 consecutive cases of placenta accreta spectrum diagnosed and managed at the hospital between 2002 and 2017
finding: The presence of a 'rail sign' on ultrasound, defined as two parallel neovascularizations over the uterovesical junction and bladder mucosa with interconnecting bridging vessels, was significantly associated with deeper villous invasion, a higher likelihood of requiring additional perioperative interventions, and an increased risk of adverse clinical outcomes in patients with placenta accreta spectrum.
